solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine rain put paid to start of match — sit frustrated

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to put paid to it, to stop it dead

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word match is taken
frustrated letters are thwarted from their order, so sit is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture abandoned because of the weather leaves the players sitting about, thwarted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective about the weather but is part of the definition; 'put paid to' means stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch mist is a thick drizzly mist, a fine rain typical of the Scottish hills.

clue.text: One to pick off wading bird and rook?

parts.note: the snipe is a long-billed wading bird of marshes
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A question about what might target a wader and a crow, as if asking which predator hunts birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who shoots individual targets from hiding picks them off one at a time.

clue.text: Frozen food pioneer's plant

definitions.meaning: Clarence ..., the American who developed quick-freezing of food
... is a name for several small flowering plants, such as the ... primrose and speedwell

explanation.surface: It reads as a factory owned by the man who pioneered frozen food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory belonging to the pioneer; it is a flower, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the surname of the inventor of frozen food; the other is a small flowering plant's common name.

clue.text: Board in part of a castle

definitions.meaning: board as in food and lodging, one's maintenance, as in earning one's living costs
the strongest central tower of a medieval castle, the donjon

explanation.surface: Someone boards or lodges inside a section of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning one's keep means paying for board; the castle sense is its fortified central tower.

clue.text: Guard on Hampshire river in trial filming

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another places it above, so first

parts.note: a screen guards or shields something
the Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, a county in southern England

explanation.surface: A security guard stands by a Hampshire river while a film is being trialled.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a trial filming of an actor to judge suitability for a role.

clue.text: Fancy woman missing M1 — it's a worry

indicators.note: missing tells us a piece is lost from the word for the fancy woman

parts.note: a fancy woman is a lover or kept woman, a mistress
M1, Britain's main motorway north from London, is read as the letters M and I

explanation.surface: A man fretting because his lover failed to turn up via the M1 motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; here the digit 1 reads as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental tension or anxiety, something that preys on the mind.

clue.text: Woman falls in station

definitions.meaning: the ... Falls on the Zambezi river

explanation.surface: A woman takes a tumble at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions joined by 'in'; 'falls' looks like a verb but is the waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, the great African waterfall, and a London railway terminus.

clue.text: Child under small slide

indicators.note: in a down clue the child's word sits below the other piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A little child is playing beneath a small playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is an uncontrolled sliding movement, as of a car on ice.

clue.text: Swindle loaded eccentric? Kind of

indicators.note: loaded is slang for drunk, so the following letters stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A con artist cheats a wealthy oddball, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' seems to mean rich, but it is drunk, the anagram signal; ECCENTRIC and KIND OF are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidence trick is a swindle in which the victim's trust is first won and then exploited.

clue.text: Unenthusiastic in assembly about bringing in piano

indicators.note: bringing in means the reversed word takes the musical letter inside it
about signals turning the assembly word round

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A lukewarm reaction in parliament to bringing in a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DIET into TEID, which holds P.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid literally means lukewarm, and figuratively half-hearted or lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: Introduced tense editor

parts.note: the present is a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A nervous editor was introduced to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like an adjective, nervous, but it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone is to introduce them formally, as at court.

clue.text: Pantomime character spotted dog

definitions.meaning: a stock figure in a costume of diamond patches in the harlequinade of British pantomime, a festive comic stage show
a Great Dane with a white coat patched irregularly in black

explanation.surface: A pantomime figure catches sight of a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like a verb, saw; it describes the dog's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the motley-clad comic servant of the harlequinade and a patchy-coated Great Dane colouring.

clue.text: Also down, after winning move in game

indicators.note: after places the words for also and down behind the winning word

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
and means also, in addition
down here means beneath, below

explanation.surface: Feeling low after winning a move in a game sounds like a sporting commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: An up-and-under is a high kick in rugby, letting the attackers chase the ball as it falls.
explanation.definitionFit: This rugby tactic is a high hanging kick that lets the attacking side run onto the ball.

clue.text: Odd-looking brush plant

indicators.note: odd-looking letters appear strange, signalling the word brush is rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange-looking bristly plant, like a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, with several stems.

clue.text: Giving support to worker in arrears

parts.note: to be behind someone is to back or support them
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: Supporting a labourer who has fallen behind with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means late or overdue, especially with payments, so in debt.

clue.text: Simultaneously hint beer has mate reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering, so these letters lurch into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinking partner staggers about while dropping hints about beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying two things in the same breath means saying them at the same moment.

clue.text: Herb found in most of Spanish region

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped from the region's name

parts.note: Tarragona is a province of Catalonia in Spain

explanation.surface: A herb that grows mostly in one part of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic culinary herb, key to béarnaise sauce.

clue.text: Tries again heading for express train

parts.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it a second time

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the word express

explanation.surface: Someone makes another attempt to catch an express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries again' wants to be the definition; it is the wordplay, and 'train' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise, and to train someone is to drill or practise them.

clue.text: Set of cards may provide sailor occupational therapy

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A pack of cards might give a seaman something to do as therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot is a pack of illustrated cards used in fortune-telling and in games.

clue.text: Longing change of T-shirt

indicators.note: a change of the letters of T-shirt rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for a fresh T-shirt to change into.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a strong craving or desire, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Wife to lock new farm building

parts.note: dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, from duchess
to bar a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A wife is told to lock up the new farm building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' meaning wife is London Cockney slang, short for duchess.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch barn is an open-sided farm shed with a curved roof, used for storing hay.

clue.text: Stan the Man's uplifting song

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so Stan the Man holds the letters within his name

explanation.surface: A celebrated performer's rousing signature song.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifting' tempts a reversal; the letters run forwards in 'Stan the Man'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song of celebration or loyalty, such as a national hymn.

clue.text: Shopkeeper burst into tears

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper suddenly started crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst into tears' reads as one idiom; 'burst' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shopkeeper selling paper, pens and other writing materials.

clue.text: Reliable worker missing in Santa Fe

indicators.note: missing signals that the insect is lost from the city name

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A dependable employee has gone missing in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means secure and dependable, something that can be relied upon.

clue.text: Tear off, gaining speed

definitions.note: a ... of travel is its speed

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of tear are set out of order

explanation.surface: Someone rips something away while gathering pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear off' reads as ripping; 'off' is the anagram signal and 'gaining' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate of travel is its pace or velocity, as in miles per hour.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: It reads as a lengthy letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective for the letter; it is a verb, yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, H.

clue.text: Throughout most of term, terribly strict

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so the phrase is rearranged

parts.note: stern means strict, severe

explanation.surface: A teacher was dreadfully strict for most of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' looks like a trimming signal, but all of MOST OF TERM is the fodder for 'terribly', giving FROMSTEMTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means from one end of a ship to the other, hence completely or throughout.
